name: Paracetamol
description: A common painkiller used to treat aches and pain. It can also be used to reduce a high temperature (fever).

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content:
Adults: Take 1-2 tablets (500mg each) every 4 to 6 hours as needed.
Do not exceed 8 tablets (4,000mg) in 24 hours.
Take with a full glass of water. Can be taken with or without food.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Paracetamol rarely causes side effects if taken at the right dosage. Rarely, it may cause an allergic reaction (rash, swelling) or liver damage if taken in overdose.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Avoid drinking excessive amounts of alcohol while taking this medicine. Do not combine with other cold or cough medicines that already contain paracetamol to avoid overdose.

name: Ibuprofen
description: An everyday painkiller for a range of aches and pains, including back pain, period pain, toothache, and it reduces inflammation.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content:
Adults: Take 1-2 tablets (200mg each) every 4 to 6 hours as needed.
Do not exceed 1,200mg in 24 hours without consulting a doctor.
Best taken with food or a glass of milk to reduce stomach upset.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content:
• Nausea or vomiting
• Mild stomach pain
• Heartburn
• Dizziness

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Do not take if you have a history of stomach ulcers, severe heart failure, or are highly allergic to aspirin. May interact with blood thinners.

name: Amoxicillin
description: A penicillin antibiotic used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections, such as middle ear infections, strep throat, and pneumonia.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content:
Dosage is prescribed by a doctor based on the infection. Typically 250mg to 500mg every 8 hours, or 500mg to 875mg every 12 hours.
You must complete the entire course of medication even if you feel better.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content:
• Nausea or vomiting
• Diarrhea
• Mild skin rash

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Do not use if you are allergic to penicillin. Seek immediate emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction: hives, difficult breathing, swelling of your face.

name: Loratadine
description: Used to treat symptoms of allergies, such as sneezing, watery eyes, and runny nose. It is non-drowsy for most people.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content:
Adults: Take 1 tablet (10mg) once daily.
Do not take more than 1 tablet in 24 hours.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content:
• Headache
• Dry mouth
• Feeling tired or drowsy (rare, but possible)

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Check with your doctor before taking if you have liver or kidney disease. Safe for use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.

name: Omeprazole
description: A proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that decreases the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Treats acid reflux and ulcers.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content:
Adults: Take 1 capsule (20mg) once daily before a meal, usually in the morning.
Swallow whole; do not crush or chew.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content:
• Headache
• Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
• Gas

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Long-term use may increase the risk of bone fractures and vitamin B12 deficiency. May interact with blood thinners or methotrexate.
